evals.name: technical-questions
evals.prompt:
Here's a JD I'm interviewing for next week. Give me the questions they'd ask in the technical round.

---
Senior Backend Engineer — Payments Platform
Ledgerly (Series B fintech, ~120 people, London/remote)

We process card and bank payments for marketplaces across the UK and EU. The Payments Platform team owns the money-movement core: authorisation, capture, refunds, payouts and reconciliation.

What you'll do
- Design and build Go services that move money reliably at scale (tens of millions of transactions/month)
- Own the ledger and reconciliation pipeline end to end
- Work with Kafka for event-driven flows between payment, risk and payout services
- Improve observability and on-call health for the platform
- Mentor mid-level engineers and lead technical design reviews

What we're looking for
- 5+ years backend experience, 2+ in Go
- Deep experience with Postgres in high-write workloads
- You've operated distributed systems in production and have opinions about idempotency, retries and exactly-once semantics
- Comfortable with ambiguity; we're still building the process around the product
- Bonus: PCI-DSS, open banking, or double-entry accounting experience

Our stack: Go, Postgres, Kafka, Kubernetes on AWS, Datadog, Terraform.
evals.expected_output: A role profile file and a technical round file with 8-10 questions specific to Go, Postgres high-write, Kafka, payments/idempotency/reconciliation, calibrated to senior. Each question has why-they-ask, strong-answer bullets, and follow-ups.
assertions: A role profile is written that states seniority as senior and lists Go, Postgres, Kafka and the payments domain
A technical round file exists with between 8 and 10 numbered questions
Every question has a 'why they ask it' line, strong-answer bullets, and at least one follow-up
At least 6 questions reference something specific from the JD (Go, Postgres high-write, Kafka, idempotency, reconciliation, ledger, payouts, refunds, PCI)
No question is a generic textbook or trivia question that could be asked unchanged at any company (e.g. 'explain message queues', 'what is a goroutine')
No question leaks its own answer in the wording (e.g. names the race condition it is asking the candidate to find)
Questions are calibrated to senior: at least 3 probe judgment or trade-offs rather than recall

evals.name: take-home-scaffold
evals.prompt:
Generate a take-home test for this role. I'll do it tonight and want you to review it after.

Mid-level Frontend Engineer (React / TypeScript)
Rosterly — scheduling software for hospitality teams

Rosterly helps restaurants and bars build staff rotas, track hours and manage shift swaps. You'll join a team of 4 frontend engineers working on the manager-facing web app.

Responsibilities
- Build and maintain features in our React + TypeScript app (Vite, React Query, Tailwind)
- Work closely with product and design to ship weekly
- Write tests with Vitest and React Testing Library
- Improve performance of data-heavy views (rota grids with hundreds of shifts)

Requirements
- 2-4 years with React and TypeScript
- Solid understanding of state management and data fetching patterns
- Experience with forms, validation and optimistic UI
- Care about accessibility and keyboard navigation
- Nice to have: experience with drag-and-drop UIs, date/time handling across timezones
evals.expected_output: A take-home directory with BRIEF.md, README.md, a hidden .rubric/RUBRIC.md, and a minimal runnable Vite+React+TS starter with Vitest set up. The task is a scheduling/rota domain slice with one hard part (e.g. shift overlap or timezone), an intentionally ambiguous requirement, and a 3-4 hour budget.
assertions: A take-home directory contains BRIEF.md, README.md, and a rubric in a hidden .rubric/ directory
A runnable Vite + React + TypeScript starter exists with Vitest configured and at least one test file
The scaffold's tests pass when run (npm install && npm test or equivalent)
BRIEF.md states a time budget of roughly 3 to 4 hours
The task is in the rota/scheduling/hospitality domain, not a generic todo app
BRIEF.md contains at least one intentionally underspecified requirement, and RUBRIC.md scores whether the candidate noticed and documented a decision on it
RUBRIC.md identifies one hard part and weights it more heavily than other criteria
The final message tells the user not to read the rubric until they finish and how to trigger the review

evals.name: three-round-loop
evals.prompt:
run me through 3 interviews for this posting. I want to see what each round would look like.

Data Engineer II
Northwind Health (US healthcare analytics, 800 employees)

About the team: The Data Platform team builds the pipelines that power clinical and claims analytics for 40+ hospital systems. We ingest HL7/FHIR feeds, claims files and EHR extracts into a Snowflake warehouse.

You will:
- Build and operate batch and streaming pipelines with Airflow, dbt and Spark on Databricks
- Model clinical and claims data for analytics consumers
- Implement data quality checks and lineage
- Handle PHI in compliance with HIPAA
- Partner with analysts and clinical informaticists to understand requirements

You have:
- 3-5 years in data engineering
- Strong SQL and Python
- Experience with dbt, Airflow, Spark or similar
- Understanding of dimensional modeling
- Bonus: healthcare data (HL7, FHIR, claims), Snowflake, Great Expectations
evals.expected_output: A role profile and three round files (likely technical, data modeling/system design, behavioural) that build on each other, calibrated to mid-level, specific to healthcare data, HIPAA, dbt/Airflow/Spark. No repeated questions across rounds. Since there is no live user, the mock is not simulated.
assertions: A role profile is written that states mid-level (Data Engineer II) and healthcare/HIPAA/HL7/FHIR/Snowflake/dbt/Airflow context
Exactly three round files exist, each a different round type

Question-based rounds (technical, behavioural, screen) have why-they-ask, strong-answer bullets and follow-ups on every question; a system design round instead has a prompt plus clarifying questions, core components, hard parts, and failure and trade-off probes
No question text is repeated across the three rounds
Later rounds reference or build on earlier ones (e.g. design round references the technical round's topics, behavioural maps to signals from the profile)
The behavioural round explicitly maps each question to a signal extracted from the posting
The output does not simulate a fake candidate answering; it presents the rounds as material and notes a live mock needs a session
At least 5 questions across the rounds mention healthcare-specific concerns (PHI, HIPAA, claims, HL7/FHIR, clinical data)

evals.name: topic-drill
evals.prompt: quiz me on caching. I'm going for senior backend roles and I always get caught out on the tricky stuff. don't go easy
evals.expected_output: A topic profile and one technical round on caching at senior level with a chosen domain, 8-10 questions including marked curveballs, covering several caching sub-areas, with the chat message naming topics only.
assertions: A short profile is written stating topic (caching), level (senior) and a chosen domain used consistently across the questions
A round file with 8 to 10 numbered questions exists, each with why-they-ask, strong-answer bullets and follow-ups
At least 3 questions are marked as curveballs and belong to a recognisable trap type (obvious answer wrong, predict the output, find the flaw, ask before answering)

The questions cover at least 4 distinct caching sub-areas (e.g. invalidation, consistency, stampedes/thundering herd, TTL choice, what not to cache, cache-aside vs write-through, eviction, negative caching)
Questions are anchored in a concrete domain scenario rather than textbook phrasing (no bare 'explain cache-aside')
Questions are calibrated to senior: they probe trade-offs and failure modes, not definitions
The final chat message lists topics but does not summarise or reveal answers
Since the user said 'quiz me' and no live answers are possible, the output does not simulate a fake candidate; it presents the questions and offers to run them live
